\paragraph{Goodhart effects.}
Repurposed as a training signal, $r = r_{\text{exec}} \cdot (1 + \beta\,\text{ISR})$, ISR is gamed at its own definition---a Goodhart effect where the diagnostic becomes the optimization target~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy, karwowski-goodhart-rl, gao-reward-overoptimization}.
On FOLIO, this instantiates \emph{regressional} Goodhart~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy}: $P{\to}P$ tautologies yield $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ by construction, so ISR erroneously rewards the shortcut it was designed to detect.
At $\beta{=}0.1$, ISR amplifies H7 tautological collapse ${\sim}5{\times}$ (70.6\% vs.\ 13.7\% random, Fisher $p{<}10^{-38}$); the sole apparent ISR advantage reduces to $1.06\times$ after controlling for a premise-count confound.
At $\beta{\geq}0.2$, \emph{extremal} Goodhart dominates: training destabilizes regardless of signal source (ISR $66{\pm}42\%$, random $54{\pm}35\%$ at $\beta{=}0.3$).
On ProofFOL, hacking constructions yield $\text{ISR}{=}0.0$, so ISR correctly penalizes shortcuts, producing beneficial instability (76.8\% vs.\ 17.4\% genuine, $p{=}0.10$)---not Goodhart but dataset-dependent success.
ISR's asymmetry is the central finding: \emph{reliable as observer, dataset-dependent as optimizer.}

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

STA exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides, while SFT localizes the failure to RL (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
As a diagnostic, ISR is the strongest contribution of this work---it requires no annotations, applies to any solver-backed formalization, and surfaces failure modes (H7b obfuscated tautology, query-as-fact gaming) that text-match classifiers miss.

Repurposed as a training signal, ISR produces dataset-dependent outcomes determined by hacking geometry: on FOLIO, Goodhart effects amplify H7 ${\sim}5{\times}$ ($p{<}10^{-39}$) and transfer to Prolog (3/3 seeds, 0\% non-hacking; \S\ref{sec:crosslogic}); on ProofFOL, beneficial instability yields lower prove rates but 76.8\% vs.\ 17.4\% genuine ($p{=}0.10$; \S\ref{sec:crossdomain}).
Our deconfounding analysis further shows that ISR's sole apparent reward advantage reduces to $1.06\times$ after controlling for premise count---a simple length penalty may achieve comparable effects (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}).

ISR's vulnerability is not inherent---it depends on whether dataset-specific shortcuts satisfy the metric's LOO structure.
Where hacking yields $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ (FOLIO: $P{\to}P$ tautologies), ISR erroneously rewards shortcuts; where it does not (ProofFOL: hacking yields $\text{ISR}{=}0.0$), ISR correctly penalizes them.
This asymmetry suggests that mitigation should target the structural vulnerability rather than abandoning the metric: component-count normalization (controlling the LOO bias), reward ensembling with orthogonal signals, or constrained optimization that caps ISR-rewarded prove rate.

Computationally, LOO ablation requires $n$ solver calls per proved sample ($n{=}6$--$19$ in our experiments); an $O(1)$ binary variant achieves near-identical diagnostic discrimination but introduces a training-time confound (Appendix~\ref{app:o1-ablation}).

\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

STA exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides, while SFT localizes the failure to RL (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
As a diagnostic requiring no annotations, ISR surfaces failure modes (H7b obfuscated tautology, query-as-fact gaming) that text-match classifiers miss.
Repurposed as a training signal, ISR produces dataset-dependent outcomes: on FOLIO, Goodhart effects amplify H7 ${\sim}5{\times}$ ($p{<}10^{-39}$); on ProofFOL, beneficial instability yields 76.8\% vs.\ 17.4\% genuine ($p{=}0.10$).
Our deconfounding analysis reduces ISR's sole apparent reward advantage to $1.06\times$---a simple length penalty may suffice (\S\ref{sec:goodhart}).

ISR's vulnerability is not inherent---it depends on whether dataset-specific shortcuts satisfy the metric's LOO structure: where hacking yields $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$ (FOLIO), ISR rewards shortcuts; where it does not (ProofFOL, $\text{ISR}{=}0.0$), ISR penalizes them.
Mitigation should target this structural vulnerability---component-count normalization, reward ensembling, or constrained optimization---rather than abandoning the metric.
Computationally, LOO ablation costs $n$ solver calls per sample ($n{=}6$--$19$); an $O(1)$ variant achieves comparable diagnostic discrimination (Appendix~\ref{app:o1-ablation}).
